The γ′ phase cuboids (the darker contrast phase) are uniform in size (~400 nm in average), regular in shape, and well aligned along <100> directions.
The γ phase forms narrow and continuous channels in between the γ′ phase cuboids, with an average channel width of 70 nm.
The γ′ phase cuboids have evolved into an N-type rafted structure. No TCP phase was detected in this sample.

For the case of pre-straining under tension along [001] (the first column, type II), more dislocations are seen on the horizontal γ′/γ interface (001) (Fig. 4(a)) than on the vertical interfaces (010) and (100) (Fig. 4(e), (i)).

For pre-straining in compression along [001] (the second column, type III), more dislocations are formed on the vertical interfaces (010) and (100) (Fig. 4(f), (j)) than on the horizontal interface (001) (Fig. 4(b)).

For pre-straining in compression along the lateral direction [010] (the third column, type IV), more dislocations are formed on the interfaces parallel to the loading axis, i.e. (100) (Fig. 4(k)) and (001) (Fig. 4(c)), than the interface perpendicular to the loading axis, i.e., (010) (Fig. 4(g)).

attributes.morphology: networked in (001) plane; dislocation pairs on (010) plane

evidence.quote: The dislocations are networked in the (001) plane and remain mostly in the γ phase at the interface. The average cell size of the (001) dislocation network is ~ 40 nm in both sample. On the (010) plane, they are mostly dislocation pairs, implying that they have mostly penetrated into the γ′ phase.
